items.title: Ghaziabad administration orders unsealing of madrasa after Allahabad High Court directive

State of UP & Ors]. The District Minority Welfare Officer (DMWO), Ghaziabad ordered local administration and waqf officials to restore possession, citing the High Court's conditional directive that required the seal's removal in the absence of an adverse order within two weeks. The order was passed in compliance with a ruling by the Allahabad High Court on October 30, 2026, in a writ petition challenging the administrative action. While disposing of the plea, the High Court had directed the competent State authority to decide the matter within a two-week window after providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner. The Court had clarified: "In case no adverse order is passed against the petitioner within above period, the seal affixed to the premises of the petitioner's Madarsa shall be removed- Otherwise legal consequence of order if passed shall follow." The submission was made during the hearing of a a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition seeking the immediate appointment of an Advocate General for the Union Territory. Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli last week submitted that the appointment process is underway and would be completed within a month. items.title: Manipur High Court keeps Census 2027 on hold amid concerns over displaced persons, population records
items.summary: The Manipur High Court has directed that the Census 2027 exercise in the State remain suspended until April 30, 2027, while the Central government considers representations raising concerns over the exercise amid the prevailing situation in the State [ KSA Vs Union of India ]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice M Sundar and Justice A Guneshwar Sharma directed the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India to consider seven representations and pass a reasoned order by April 30, 2027. The Court ordered that the notifications keeping the Census exercise in abeyance should continue to operate without modification until that date. " To put it differently, the census exercise for the State of Manipur will continue to be put on hold/kept in abeyance till 30.04.2027 ," the Bench said. The Court further directed that the Census exercise remain suspended for four weeks after the authorities decide the representations, allowing aggrieved parties to challenge the decision. items.title: Bengaluru grindstone murders: Five of seven victims found, two bodies recovered in Mysuru
items.summary: Bengaluru police recovered two more bodies on Sunday, November 8, in the murder of seven members of a family. The remains, suspected to be those of the accused man’s elder brother Shivakumar and his wife Divya, were found near Chamundi Hills in Mysuru. Police took the accused, S Indushekhar (52), to the forest area between Tavarekatte and Chamundi Hills to identify the spot where he allegedly dumped the bodies. They were found around 500 metres apart. With Sunday's recovery, five of the seven victims have been found. Indushekhar has been accused of killing his wife Sunitha, her mother Roopavati, her brothers Shivakumar and Shankar, their wives Divya and Nalini, and Shivakumar’s seven-year-old son Puneeth. The bodies of Indushekhar's wife Sunitha (40) and mother-in-law Roopavathi were recovered from a forest in Salem district, Tamil Nadu, on Saturday. The body of Puneeth was earlier found near the foothills of Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur district and has since been cremated. The police said the bodies recovered in Mysuru would undergo postmortem examinations before being handed over to relatives. items.title: She lost her father. Now she is fighting the powerful for justice
items.summary: Jayabalakrishnan (55), a small eatery owner in Ernakulam’s Cheranallur, was killed on October 25 after his scooter was struck by a car driven by a sessions judge’s minor son. Now the family is fighting to secure justice. They alleged that the judge used his influence and destroyed crucial evidence. The family began their protest minutes after Jayabalakrishnan’s body was cremated as the arrested minor was released on station bail under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act. They held a protest in front of the police station, and later he was taken back into custody; on October 26, the Juvenile Justice Board granted him bail. Later, the police booked the judge under the relevant sections of the Motor Vehicles Act, as the car was registered under his name. On October 31, the family also filed a complaint with the Cheranallur police, alleging that evidence such as the exact position of the vehicle, the condition of the accident site, marks on the road, blood stains, CCTV footage, and eyewitnesses, which are crucial to the investigation, might have been altered. items.title: On Sunday walks along Ludhiana’s Buddha Darya, a citizens’ group counts what is left to fix
items.summary: Every Sunday morning, Colonel Chander Mohan Lakhanpal walks beside the Buddha Darya in Ludhiana. In his walk, which is part exercise, part inspection, he is joined by fellow team members of the Public Action Committee , a non-government organisation working to restore Punjab’s natural resources. Lakhanpal watches the Darya—a 47-kilometre-long seasonal stream and a tributary of the Sutlej river—and documents what industries discharge into it. He shares with pride that in November 2022, they had identified 370 discharge points in their ‘ padyatra ’ (march) along the water stream; now just 15 of those are left. “Our regular watch has ensured that unauthorised discharge points are shut.” But the Public Action Committee has more to do, Lakhanpal says. Several of the remaining discharge points are in the stretch recognised as polluted , requiring restoration, by the Central Pollution Control Board in 2025. On such walks, he said he often notices foam floating over the Darya at even ‘authorised’ discharge points.
